rationale.selected_because: The immediate objective is to secure the newly available 15 January diagnostic visit before its 17:30 booking deadline, while obtaining Leah’s required direct access confirmation. The latest report says the living room is now 10°C and no appointment or interim arrangement is confirmed. I propose the inspection under the landlord’s conditional urgent-repair authority, expressly preserving that it may be used only if the incident is treated as qualifying urgent repair. In parallel, clarify whether the niece’s room is actually usable, coordinate a no-commitment supplier check, and seek separate landlord spending approval for any interim provision.

Urgent-repair classification is a supported operational inference from the worsening cold, lack of safe temporary heat, and delayed standard visit; the cited authority remains conditional on that classification.
assumptions: The successive references to the heating failure and diagnostic visit concern the same ongoing case-local repair, based on the continuous chronology and parties; this does not resolve any extraction uncertainty.
The proposed inspection is limited to the £168 diagnostic call-out. No repair, parts, temporary heater, transport, or accommodation spending is authorized by this proposal.
alternatives_considered: The 17 January standard offer is not a suitable fallback to rely on because Leah cannot guarantee access then.
No interim purchase or transport is proposed: the duty file establishes no separate spending limit, and the need, option, and cost are not yet confirmed.

actions.message: We have received your update. The contractor has offered a 15 January, 09:00–11:00 diagnostic slot, but it is not booked and must be secured by 17:30. We are seeking your direct access confirmation, including the call and notice arrangements. No interim arrangement is yet confirmed.
